minutes.headline: Committee eyes June 12 public forum on the draft master plan; has never approved any meeting minutes
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee heard the planning consultant's methodology for narrowing roughly 105+ community-sourced recommendations into a shortlist for the draft master plan, and pressed for clearer, more transparent criteria behind the keep/review/reject classifications. The committee worked toward setting a June public engagement meeting (tentatively June 12 at Smoke Stack Roasters) and assigned tasks for venue confirmation and advertising, while also surfacing procedural gaps -- an outdated member roster, unclear swearing-in status, and the discovery that the committee has never formally approved any past meeting minutes.

what_happened.line: Committee pressed the planning consultant for clearer, more transparent criteria behind how recommendations are sorted into keep, review, or reject.
Committee tentatively set a public forum on the draft master plan for June 12 at Smoke Stack Roasters, pending venue confirmation.
Committee discovered it has never formally approved any of its past meeting minutes and added a catch-up plan to the next agenda.
Consultant said the low/medium/high budget rankings attached to each recommendation are rough order-of-magnitude estimates, not precise figures.
A poll will go out to schedule the committee's next meeting in May rather than fixing a date in the room.

why_it_matters: The shortlisting method now under scrutiny will determine which community-submitted ideas make it into the draft master plan residents get asked to weigh in on.
The June 12 forum, if confirmed, is the public's chance to react to that draft before it goes to Town Meeting in November.
Cost estimates tied to each recommendation are described by the consultant as rough brackets, not budget figures a resident should rely on for planning.
